Based on the provided evidence, the patient underwent an echocardiogram (ECHO). The report explicitly states: "Funzione sistolica globale ai limiti inferiori della norma (FE stimata intorno al 45%)" which translates to global systolic function at the lower limits of normal (estimated EF around 45%). According to the Brighton criteria synonyms provided, a decreased ejection fraction constitutes "New focal or diffuse left or right ventricular function abnormalities". Additionally, the report notes "modeste alterazioni segmentarie della cinetica" (modest segmental kinetic alterations), which corresponds to "Segmental wall motion abnormalities". The report also mentions "lievi irregolarità dello spessore parietale" (slight irregularities of wall thickness), which maps to "Wall thickness change".

The evidence explicitly states "Pericardio indenne" (Pericardium unharmed/intact) and "Non valvulopatie di rilievo significativo", ruling out pericardial effusion/inflammation. The report suggests the findings are compatible with ischemic injury ("possibile natura ischemica") rather than confirming myocarditis, so options confirming myocarditis or pericarditis are incorrect. There is no mention of ventricular dilation (the left ventricle is described as "normali dimensioni").

Therefore, the applicable findings from the echocardiogram are functional abnormalities (reduced EF), segmental wall motion abnormalities, and wall thickness changes.
